title: PLAN LOCK 1/3 — Single Sign-On + Permission system (ระบบล็อกอินและสิทธิ์)
detail: Declared by owner 2026-07-08 as the first of 3 gate tasks (registry/CONSTITUTION.json iron_rules: no new Module/Page/Feature until all 3 are DONE 100%). Renumbered from TASK-023 to TASK-001 same day per owner's explicit instruction — see CURRENT_STATE.json → plan_lock.renumbering_note for the full ID mapping (the OLD TASK-001/002/003 now live at TASK-026/027/028). Goal: log in once (SSO), reach every Portal and every API with that one session. Scope: wire Supabase Auth end-to-end across Admin Login, User Login, Partner Login, Business Portal Login, API Token Login; one shared session for the whole system; middleware auth-check on every route; Role set = Super Admin/Admin/Employee/Partner/Customer/AI Service; a Permission Registry; Route Guards; logout across every system; refresh token; remember-login. Definition of Done (all required): login once reaches every Portal; API calls share the one session; no duplicate/parallel login pages; every API route passes requireAuth. Sequenced before TASK-002/003 because both depend on the same session model. Note: zero Supabase Auth users exist in production today (see TASK-022) — this task is also the real fix for that gap, not a separate effort.
progress_note_2026_07_15: Real security audit performed: 76 total API routes, 55 had requireAuth before this pass. Found and fixed 9 real gaps: app/api/command (CRITICAL — unauthenticated POST could trigger the real cognitive command pipeline) + 8 real info/source-disclosure routes (build, deploy, governance, dbd, traces, routes, self-description, reader — reader was the most severe, a full source-code file reader across the entire codebase). Now 64/76 protected. Remaining 12 unauthenticated are legitimately public by design (owner-confirmed via AskUserQuestion): auth/logout, connectors oauth authorize/callback, connectors webhook, 7 app/api/v1/* self-description routes, manual-doc (a 501 stub). TASK-001 Definition of Done (every API route passes requireAuth) is now effectively met for all routes that SHOULD require it — the remaining 12 are intentional exceptions, not gaps. Still open for full TASK-001 completion: session model verification across all 5 login surfaces (Admin/User/Partner/Business/API Token), remember-login, refresh token behavior, and confirming zero duplicate/parallel login pages — not audited in this pass.

title: Vercel Deployment Protection (SSO) is blocking public access to the production site
blocked_on: system owner — real access-control decision, not something to flip silently
detail: Discovered 2026-07-08 (DNA-000018) immediately after deploying to production: every route, including fully public pages like / and /login, returns 302 to https://vercel.com/sso-api — this is Vercel's own Deployment Protection / Vercel Authentication project setting, unrelated to middleware.ts (which only ever gated /admin/*). No real visitor (customer, partner) can reach the site without a Vercel account added to this team. Configure at: Vercel Dashboard → dna-os-deadboard project → Settings → Deployment Protection → turn off 'Vercel Authentication' for Production (or scope it as needed). See TASK-020 for a related gap worth fixing first or alongside this. UPDATE 2026-07-08: the API-auth gap this task was waiting on (TASK-020) is now fixed — every /api/admin/* route checks its own admin_session cookie regardless of Deployment Protection. The owner can now disable Deployment Protection without that specific risk; still an access-control decision only the owner should make (Vercel Dashboard → dna-os-deadboard → Settings → Deployment Protection).

title: Several /api/admin/* routes have no auth check of their own — only ever protected by page-level gates
detail: Found during this session's earlier audits, resurfaced 2026-07-08 while evaluating TASK-019: routes like /api/admin/partners and /api/admin/jobs (unlike the connectors/upload/notifications routes built this session, which all call requireAdmin() checking the admin_session cookie) don't check auth themselves — they've only ever been shielded by (a) Vercel's Deployment Protection wall and (b) middleware.ts gating the /admin page that normally calls them. Neither actually protects the API route if hit directly. Should be fixed by adding the same requireAdmin() pattern (see app/api/admin/connectors/route.ts or app/api/admin/upload/route.ts for the exact pattern) to every /api/admin/* route that's missing it — especially before/alongside disabling TASK-019's Deployment Protection, since that removes the last layer currently shielding these routes in production. RESOLVED 2026-07-08 (DNA-000019, Production QA mission): added the same requireAdmin() cookie-check pattern to all 16 previously-unprotected /api/admin/* handlers (backup, debt-trackings x3, documents x3, partners x4, pulse, settings GET, transactions x3). backup/route.ts was the most severe instance — it returned a full unauthenticated dump of every business table.

title: Upload feature — built and live
detail: Built 2026-07-07 (DNA-000017), after the owner's follow-up narrowed the pause condition to 'missing credential' only (no credential was missing for this one, so proceeded): created a private 'attachments' Storage bucket in the live Supabase project (supabase/migrations/20260707000002_attachments_bucket.sql, applied via supabase db query --linked, verified present via a SELECT against storage.buckets). Built app/api/admin/upload/route.ts (admin_session-gated POST/GET/DELETE — upload, 5-minute signed-URL fetch, delete; 20MB size cap; PDF/PNG/JPEG/WEBP/HEIC allow-list) and components/documents/FileUpload.tsx (reusable, no business-specific logic), wired into components/documents/DocumentBuilder.tsx as a real 'attach a reference file' section on every document type (invoice/receipt/PO/delivery-order/debt-notice/etc., since they all share this one component). Attachment listing uses Supabase Storage's own .list() by documentId-prefixed folder — no new DB table needed. Scope was deliberately kept to 'attach a file to a document' (the one universally-applicable, non-guessed use case across every real document type already in the system) rather than a generic unscoped uploader. npm run build clean (exit 0), and confirmed both new API routes correctly return 401 without the admin_session cookie (same auth pattern as the connectors routes).
